highlight.title: Revelio Labs: Monopsony in the US Labor Market — Is Worker Power Back?
highlight.summary: US workers now retain ~80 cents of each marginal dollar earned, up from ~70 cents pre-2022, with variation by industry, union status, and AI exposure — providing a direct wage-share signal linked to AI adoption.

extractedStats.overlayLabel: AI-exposed occupations saw faster markdown declines post-2023
extractedStats.quote: markdowns are smaller in more unionized occupations and have fallen faster in occupations more exposed to AI

extractedStats.overlayLabel: Avg earnings markdowns fell from ~30% pre-2022 to ~20% in 2023-2025
extractedStats.quote: average earnings markdowns fell from about 30% before 2022 to about 20% in 2023-2025

extractedStats.overlayLabel: Higher AI exposure correlates with larger markdown reductions post-2022
extractedStats.quote: Scatter plot of within-occupation change in markdowns between pre-AI (2016-2022) and post-AI (2023-2025) periods against AI exposure score among occupations.

highlight.title: Beyond the Laggard Myth: Time-Series Analysis of AI Job Market Dynamics in Construction
highlight.summary: One of the first cross-industry time-series analyses of AI job postings in construction, benchmarking AI hiring growth against digital and traditional sectors to challenge linear diffusion assumptions.

highlight.title: NY Fed Liberty Street Economics: Evaluating New LinkedIn Labor Market Tightness Indicators
highlight.summary: The NY Fed evaluates LinkedIn-derived labor market tightness measures as real-time alternatives to JOLTS, providing new high-frequency job-seeker-to-opening ratios with implications for wage pressure forecasts.

highlight.title: NBER: Saving for the Machines — Task Models, Capital Accumulation, and Automation Growth
highlight.summary: In a standard task model, capital supply governs the magnitude of automation-driven growth; the paper argues task-structure shifts alter returns to machine accumulation, with implications for labor's share as automation expands.

extractedStats.overlayLabel: Automation growth boom: 11.7% annual growth under optimal saving vs 2.2% fixed rate
extractedStats.quote: the same technology path that generates 11.7% annual growth when households choose their saving rate optimally delivers only 2.2% when the saving rate is fixed at the calibrated U.S. 2025 level of 23%

extractedStats.overlayLabel: Hand-to-mouth households lose 40–67% of consumption equivalent from automation
extractedStats.quote: hand-to-mouth households lose the equivalent of two-fifths to two-thirds of their consumption, while keeping them on trend temporarily costs at most a fifth of GDP

extractedStats.overlayLabel: Machines perform growing share of tasks; task structure sets wage evolution path
extractedStats.quote: When machines can perform a growing share of tasks, growth depends on two margins: how the task structure affects the returns to accumulating machines, and how strongly capital accumulation responds to those returns

extractedStats.overlayLabel: Task structure governs duration of automation growth boom and wage evolution
extractedStats.quote: the task structure sets the duration of this growth boom and the evolution of wages

highlight.title: NBER: Public R&D and the Automation of Manufacturing — Evidence from the Space Race
highlight.summary: Space Race–era public R&D measurably shifted US manufacturing toward automation, providing historical causal evidence that government-funded technology investment accelerates physical-task displacement.

highlight.title: The Global AI Divide: Cross-National Analysis of AI Integration and Labor Market Inequality
highlight.summary: Cross-national analysis finds AI adoption generates productivity gains while intensifying structural labor-market inequalities, with differential impacts across income groups and geographies.

highlight.title: Indeed Hiring Lab: US Labor Market Snapshot — October 2026
highlight.summary: Monthly snapshot covering US job postings, wages, unemployment, and openings as of October 2026, flagging current directional trends across key labor-market indicators.

extractedStats.overlayLabel: Posted wage growth 2.4% YoY, below CPI inflation of 3.7% (real wage decline)
extractedStats.quote: Posted wage growth is 2.4% year-over-year, against CPI inflation of 3.7%.

extractedStats.overlayLabel: AI-related postings at 7.3% of all postings, up from 3.3% peak in 2022
extractedStats.quote: AI-related postings make up 7.3% of all postings, past their previous peak of 3.3% in 2022.

extractedStats.overlayLabel: Software Development sector JPI lowest among tracked sectors at ~79

highlight.title: What is Work For? Labor, Politics, and Meaning in the Age of AI — Cross-National Survey
highlight.summary: Original survey of 8,234 working-age adults across UK, US, Denmark, and India quantifies non-monetary motivations for work and attitudes toward AI-driven job change, with cross-national breakdowns.

extractedStats.overlayLabel: 81% of 8,234 surveyed workers report job satisfaction across UK/US/Denmark/India
extractedStats.quote: I find that 81% of respondents report being satisfied with their job, and a majority across all four countries are strongly motivated by the non-monetary components of their employment.

extractedStats.overlayLabel: 1/3 of workers intrinsically motivated by job role itself; ~25% by social/community aspects
extractedStats.quote: one third of working respondents are motivated intrinsically by their job--valuing their role for its own sake. Nearly one quarter are driven by social and community-related aspects of their employment, 17% by social status, and just over one quarter by the transactional financial benefits of their job.

extractedStats.overlayLabel: 1/5 of workers would stay in role even if offered 120% salary as guaranteed income
extractedStats.quote: one fifth of workers would stay even if offered up to 120% of their salary.

extractedStats.overlayLabel: Non-monetary work motivations evenly distributed across income and collar lines
extractedStats.quote: these non-monetary work motivations are evenly distributed across the income distribution and between white- and blue-collar workers.
